currentContext.strengths: Asset-light growth model (JDA / JV / Development Manager) that keeps upfront land investment low while applying MICL's own execution strength across every project|Distinct niche in redevelopment of private societies, MHADA societies, cluster development and SRA projects across MMR, with a strong track record in high-rise towers|Over six decades of construction history; Group has delivered 60+ million sq. ft. of construction, 60+ projects and 20,000+ units, backed by 500+ in-house engineers|Fully integrated in-house EPC capability (own plant, machinery and manpower) covering ports through high-rise residential, allowing construction value to be captured within the Group as the real-estate pipeline converts to execution|Track record of delivering every real-estate project ahead of schedule and nearly fully sold out, with projects typically ~90% sold by the time they receive their Occupation Certificate|Net debt free at consolidated level (March 2026) with a CARE A+ (stable outlook) credit rating and healthy liquidity, enabling project acquisition from internal accruals
currentContext.strategies: Continue the asset-light growth model — collaborating with landowners and partners via Joint Development Agreements, Joint Ventures and the Development Manager model instead of outright land acquisition — to keep upfront investment low while applying MICL's execution strength|Deepen presence in Mumbai's prestige luxury micro-markets (South Mumbai — Tardeo, Marine Lines; Bandra — BKC, Pali Hill, off-Bandstand) through selective acquisitions|Pursue 'Vision 2031': double the real estate portfolio to a GDV of ₹35,000+ crores over the next five years, funded with discipline rather than leverage|Introduce 'MS Collection', a new ultra-luxury vertical for boutique, sea-view developments at the Group's most distinguished addresses|Grow the in-house EPC engine so that, as the real-estate launch pipeline converts to execution, a greater share of construction is delivered in-house and value is retained within the Group|Expand beyond India through MICL Global's growing presence in Florida, USA (Miami, Miami Beach, Fort Lauderdale), with an aspiration over time to build it into a business as significant as the Indian operations|Build selective partnerships with established developers and landowners, combining MICL's execution capability with their land or scale to pursue larger opportunities than MICL could pursue alone|Fund the growth phase from a position of financial strength — net debt free, healthy liquidity, project acquisition from internal accruals, with selective construction finance drawn only as projects require|During FY26 the Company paid two interim dividends of Rs. 0.45 per equity share each (total Rs. 0.90 per share), which shareholders were asked at the AGM to confirm as the final dividend for the year; a formal Dividend Distribution Policy is maintained and posted on the Company's website. The Company states there were no materially significant related-party transactions during FY26 that had potential conflict with the Company's interest, governed by a Board-approved Policy on Materiality of Related Party Transactions.
currentContext.expansion: MICL's expansion is real-estate portfolio growth rather than plant capex: during FY26 the Group added a new South Mumbai project at Tardeo (est. GDV ~₹2,000 crores), taking the combined Tardeo/Marine Lines portfolio past ₹8,000 crores, and launched its BKC project 'Artek Park' (GDV ~₹850 crores) at Bandra Kurla Complex. Subsequent to year-end, the Group acquired a third Bandra micro-market project — an ultra-luxury sea-view development off Bandstand (est. GDV ₹1,000+ crores) — taking the combined Bandra portfolio (Artek Park + off-Bandstand + upcoming Pali Hill project) to over ₹2,350 crores. As of the report date, the ongoing/upcoming real-estate portfolio spans 12 projects with a combined GDV of ₹18,625+ crores and 5.3 million sq. ft. of carpet area, across South Mumbai (Tardeo, Marine Lines) and the western/central suburbs (Bandra, Vile Parle, Goregaon, Dahisar, Ghatkopar, Mulund). The Group is preparing to launch further projects (subject to regulatory approvals and market conditions) with a combined GDV potential of over ₹6,700 crores spanning Marine Lines, Tardeo, Pali Hill, off-Bandstand and Mulund. On the EPC/infrastructure side, the BMCT project at Nhava Sheva port is nearing completion, and the Group flags the ₹75,000+ crore Vadhavan Port project in Palghar (near Mumbai) as an infrastructure-cycle opportunity aligned with its port-EPC heritage. Internationally, MICL Global (Florida, USA) added a new development, 1250 West Avenue in Miami Beach, to its portfolio during the year.

risks.note: Real estate and EPC sectors are inherently cyclical and sensitive to changes in GDP growth, interest rates, inflation and consumer sentiment.
Non-compliance with RERA regulations, and the risk of project delays and cost overruns arising from regulatory requirements.
Project timelines may be affected by regulatory procedures, approval delays and resource availability, particularly given the Group's reliance on joint development partnerships.

Real estate projects require significant initial investment with returns expected mainly at project completion; RERA mandates that 70% of project collections be allocated to project-specific escrow accounts, and project delays can directly impact cash flows.
Cost overruns from rising material and labour costs can erode project economics if not accounted for at launch or offset through phased sales.

Actual sales may vary from projections due to changing market preferences or economic conditions, which is significant given the Company's revenue recognition is tied to the timing of launches and execution milestones.

The Group's real estate portfolio and much of its operations are concentrated within the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, making performance sensitive to local demand, regulatory and market conditions in a single metro market.

one-line thesis: Man Infra transitions from consolidation to aggressive growth with a record INR 5,600 Cr launch pipeline in FY27, shifting mix toward ultra-luxury South Mumbai projects to drive margin expansion. The company leverages a net debt-free balance sheet and strong pre-sales (90%+ in key towers) to fund this scaling, marking an inflection point for revenue recognition starting FY27.

guidance: Revenue Growth: 35-40% YoY expected in FY27; Margin: Expansion expected due to ultra-luxury mix; Order Inflow: Targeting INR 2,500 Cr sales in FY27 from new launches; Capex/Commissioning: Delivery of >1 Mn sq ft over next 6-18 months; OCs expected soon for Ghatkopar, Dahisar, Atmosphere.

segment / subsidiary detail: Real Estate: Primary driver with INR 17,500 Cr GDV across Mumbai (Tardeo, Marine Lines, BKC, etc.); FY26 Sales INR 1,800 Cr, Collections INR 990 Cr. EPC: Strategic support arm, INR 392 Cr order book, focused on ports and self-execution savings. US Ops: MICL Global holds INR 1.4 Bn (approx) GDV portfolio in Florida luxury markets.
growth verticals / optionality: Vision 2030/31 to double GDV to INR 35,000 Cr; 10+ housing societies in final negotiation for redevelopment; Launch of 'MS Collection' ultra-luxury vertical; Potential entry into commercial portfolio; FY27 launch pipeline of INR 5,600 Cr GDV.
margins & cost dynamics: Management explicitly guides for better margins in upcoming years driven by ultra-luxury projects (South Mumbai, BKC); No specific cost inflation concerns raised; Pricing power assumed flat but volume/mix driven growth.
capex / expansion: Funded via internal accruals and operating cash flows from nearing-completion projects (Ghatkopar, Dahisar, Atmosphere); No external debt raising indicated for near term; Healthy liquidity of INR 686 Cr.
capital allocation: Priority on land acquisition/redevelopment rights (10+ societies in pipeline); Debt reduction maintained (Net Debt-Free); Minority stake acquisition in US luxury project (West Avenue, Miami); Divestment not discussed.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on massive FY27 launch pipeline; Regulatory approvals for redevelopment (though mgmt cites favorable FSI policies); Market sentiment shift affecting luxury absorption; Concentration risk in Mumbai micro-markets.
management quality / tone: Highly optimistic, strategic, and confident; Emphasizes 'inflection point' and 'golden years of redevelopment'; Defensive on pricing (assumes flat prices) but bullish on volume/absorption.
non-obvious takeaways: Interest income from capital deployed in project entities is treated as a core business income stream enhancing returns; Shift from 'Aaradhya' community brand to 'MS Collection' for standalone ultra-luxury to capture different buyer psyche; EPC business increasingly used for internal cost savings on 1 Cr sq ft pipeline rather than external bidding.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Man Infraconstruction Limited (MICL Group) runs a mix of Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) and asset-light Real Estate development. The Real Estate arm builds premium-to-ultra-luxury residential and redevelopment projects (private societies, MHADA, SRA, cluster redevelopment, high-rise towers) across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, growing via Joint Development Agreements, Joint Ventures and the Development Manager model rather than outright land purchase. The EPC division executes port infrastructure, government residential and the Group's own real estate projects, and separately earns Project Management Consultancy fees on select Group projects.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India remained the fastest-growing major economy in FY26 (GDP growth of 7.6%, up from 7.1% in FY25), though growth is projected to moderate to 6.6% in FY27 amid geopolitical and trade uncertainties
- Infrastructure remains central to India's growth strategy; Union Budget 2026-27 raised public capital expenditure ~11.5% YoY, with Ports seen as one of the most compelling opportunities of the decade under the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 (targeting quadrupled port capacity by 2047); the Vadhavan Port project near Mumbai is cited as an opportunity aligned with the Group's port-EPC heritage
- India's residential real estate demand remains anchored in the premium-to-high end; the luxury/ultra-luxury segment (homes priced ₹2.5 crore and above), near-negligible in 2021, now commands close to a fifth of the market — a structural re-rating toward the high end (per ANAROCK)
- The Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) remains India's largest and deepest residential market and the epicentre of luxury/ultra-luxury demand
- Infrastructure investment (Coastal Road, expanding Metro network), the year's repo rate cut supporting affordability, and rising affluence among Mumbai's enterprise/professional class continue to strengthen MMR housing demand
- Management cautions that the pace of revenue recognition in any single year reflects the timing of launches and execution milestones rather than the underlying health of the market
- The Group's strong real estate launch pipeline is expected to translate into significant contracting opportunities for the EPC division as projects are launched
- EPC order book stood at ₹392 crore as of March 31, 2026, comprising infrastructure projects and the residential segment
- On the infrastructure side, the BMCT project at Nhava Sheva is nearing completion
- 4.4 million sq. ft. of residential construction area is under execution, comprising PMC contracts for projects at Tardeo, Vile Parle and Mulund, alongside the EPC contract at BKC
- Real estate ongoing/upcoming portfolio spans 12 projects with a combined GDV of ₹18,625+ crores and 5.3 million square feet of carpet area, from South Mumbai through prime western and central suburbs
- A meaningful share of the real-estate launch pipeline is expected to add to the EPC order book as those projects are launched

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Management explicitly guides for better margins in upcoming years driven by ultra-luxury projects (South Mumbai, BKC); No specific cost inflation concerns raised; Pricing power assumed flat but volume/mix driven growth.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority on land acquisition/redevelopment rights (10+ societies in pipeline); Debt reduction maintained (Net Debt-Free); Minority stake acquisition in US luxury project (West Avenue, Miami); Divestment not discussed.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: MICL's expansion is real-estate portfolio growth rather than plant capex: during FY26 the Group added a new South Mumbai project at Tardeo (est. GDV ~₹2,000 crores), taking the combined Tardeo/Marine Lines portfolio past ₹8,000 crores, and launched its BKC project 'Artek Park' (GDV ~₹850 crores) at Bandra Kurla Complex. Subsequent to year-end, the Group acquired a third Bandra micro-market project — an ultra-luxury sea-view development off Bandstand (est. GDV ₹1,000+ crores) — taking the combined Bandra portfolio (Artek Park + off-Bandstand + upcoming Pali Hill project) to over ₹2,350 crores. As of the report date, the ongoing/upcoming real-estate portfolio spans 12 projects with a combined GDV of ₹18,625+ crores and 5.3 million sq. ft. of carpet area, across South Mumbai (Tardeo, Marine Lines) and the western/central suburbs (Bandra, Vile Parle, Goregaon, Dahisar, Ghatkopar, Mulund). The Group is preparing to launch further projects (subject to regulatory approvals and market conditions) with a combined GDV potential of over ₹6,700 crores spanning Marine Lines, Tardeo, Pali Hill, off-Bandstand and Mulund. On the EPC/infrastructure side, the BMCT project at Nhava Sheva port is nearing completion, and the Group flags the ₹75,000+ crore Vadhavan Port project in Palghar (near Mumbai) as an infrastructure-cycle opportunity aligned with its port-EPC heritage. Internationally, MICL Global (Florida, USA) added a new development, 1250 West Avenue in Miami Beach, to its portfolio during the year.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly optimistic, strategic, and confident; Emphasizes 'inflection point' and 'golden years of redevelopment'; Defensive on pricing (assumes flat prices) but bullish on volume/absorption.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Asset-light growth model (JDA / JV / Development Manager) that keeps upfront land investment low while applying MICL's own execution strength across every project
- Distinct niche in redevelopment of private societies, MHADA societies, cluster development and SRA projects across MMR, with a strong track record in high-rise towers
- Over six decades of construction history; Group has delivered 60+ million sq. ft. of construction, 60+ projects and 20,000+ units, backed by 500+ in-house engineers
- Fully integrated in-house EPC capability (own plant, machinery and manpower) covering ports through high-rise residential, allowing construction value to be captured within the Group as the real-estate pipeline converts to execution
- Track record of delivering every real-estate project ahead of schedule and nearly fully sold out, with projects typically ~90% sold by the time they receive their Occupation Certificate
- Net debt free at consolidated level (March 2026) with a CARE A+ (stable outlook) credit rating and healthy liquidity, enabling project acquisition from internal accruals

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution risk on massive FY27 launch pipeline; Regulatory approvals for redevelopment (though mgmt cites favorable FSI policies); Market sentiment shift affecting luxury absorption; Concentration risk in Mumbai micro-markets.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Interest income from capital deployed in project entities is treated as a core business income stream enhancing returns; Shift from 'Aaradhya' community brand to 'MS Collection' for standalone ultra-luxury to capture different buyer psyche; EPC business increasingly used for internal cost savings on 1 Cr sq ft pipeline rather than external bidding.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue the asset-light growth model — collaborating with landowners and partners via Joint Development Agreements, Joint Ventures and the Development Manager model instead of outright land acquisition — to keep upfront investment low while applying MICL's execution strength
- Deepen presence in Mumbai's prestige luxury micro-markets (South Mumbai — Tardeo, Marine Lines; Bandra — BKC, Pali Hill, off-Bandstand) through selective acquisitions
- Pursue 'Vision 2031': double the real estate portfolio to a GDV of ₹35,000+ crores over the next five years, funded with discipline rather than …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising input costs or luxury demand slowdown could pressure margins despite high GDV guidance. | Competing mid-tier developers without South Mumbai land banks | loser | Med | Man Infra's pivot to ultra-luxury and massive South Mumbai pipeline may crowd out smaller players lacking similar land access or brand premium. |
| Need for rapid execution of INR 5,600 Cr launch pipeline to meet FY27 sales targets. | Premium construction material suppliers & luxury interior fit-out firms | beneficiary | High | Delivery of 1 Mn sq ft and launch of multiple luxury projects in Mumbai directly benefits high-end supply chain partners. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Accounting change] With effect from Q1 FY27 the interest earned on group funding of projects is reclassified from other income to Other Operating Revenue as ancillary to primary revenue-generating activity — ₹22.3 crores at consolidated level and ₹24.86 crores at standalone level — with comparatives reclassified under paragraph 41 of Ind AS 1; this changes the composition of reported revenue versus prior presentations.
- [Q1 FY27 milestones] Delivered Aaradhya Parkwood Towers C & D (5.3 L sq. ft. carpet, ₹925+ Cr GDV, 90%+ sold) in 45 months against a Sep-2022 launch; launched ultra-luxury Marina Vista at Pali Hill, Bandra West (0.6 L sq. ft., ₹500+ Cr GDV, 34% MICL stake) achieving 30% pre-sales commitment on launch; and secured IOA for Berkeley House.
- [Global portfolio scale] Miami/Florida portfolio of 236+ units, ~6.4 lakh sq. ft. carpet area and $1.4 Bn gross development value (project table sub-totals: ongoing 235+ units, ~6.33 L sq. ft., $1,392+ Mn GDV; completed 1 unit, ~0.06 L sq. ft., $2.5+ Mn).
- [Leadership] Board and top management detailed — Parag Shah (Chairman & Non-Executive Director, 30+ years, strategic mentor), Manan Shah (Managing Director, founded and scaled the MICL real estate business), Vatsal Shah (Non-Executive Director, leads USA strategy/execution/sales) and Ashok Mehta (Executive Director & CFO, 40+ years), with four independent directors.
